products.name: Box AI
products.note: Enterprise content AI; metadata; governance; compliance; retention policies

reading.body:
Box has built a portfolio of integrations that let AI agents handle real-world tasks: sending physical mail, managing cloud files, accessing bank data, and exchanging secrets between agents.

These Model Context Protocol tools sit at the boundary between AI systems and the infrastructure they need to operate at scale. An AI agent that can only think cannot process a loan application or onboard an employee. It must read files, verify identity, send documents, and maintain audit trails. Box's integrations bridge this gap by giving agents standardized access to storage, communication channels, and cross-agent coordination. The company's own AI product focuses on enterprise content, but this MCP registry strategy positions it as an operational layer for agentic workflows, where the binding constraint shifts from model capability to the ability to act on real data and systems.

What these integrations do not show is compute or power consumption. They are software abstractions that assume infrastructure exists elsewhere. They do show that AI scaling now depends not only on larger models and more training compute, but on standardized ways for agents to access the human-world interfaces they need to do work. For enterprises, this means the grid constraint on AI is mediated through the systems that connect agents to email, filesystems, banks, and each other.

profile_text.body:
Box is a publicly traded company, founded in 2005 and headquartered in Redwood City, CA, that provides a cloud-based content management, workflow, and collaboration platform. The company describes its offering as an Intelligent Content Management platform designed to help organizations store, share, and co-create unstructured content such as lease agreements, finance documents, sales presentations, and employee handbooks, with built-in security features including deep learning-based malware detection, automated classification, and compliance tools for standards such as GDPR, HIPAA, and FINRA.

Box AI is the company's primary AI product, tracked under the Notes, Knowledge and Meetings category, and encompasses metadata handling, governance, compliance, and retention policies. The site describes Box AI as drawing on models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google to deliver real-time summaries, deep analysis, and smart recommendations across enterprise content. The platform also includes Box AI Studio, which the company says allows developers to build and customize agents for workflow automation, and an integrated e-signature capability with unlimited e-signatures offered at no additional cost.

Box files with the SEC under ticker BOX with CIK 0001372612, and its most recently reported annual revenue, from a 10-K covering the period ending January 31, 2026, was $1,177,253,000. The held facts record 187 legal matters with California exposure but no specific cases are listed. The site holds an MCP registry presence, though the listed MCP servers are associated with third-party providers rather than Box's own infrastructure.
